blocks.text: Between-session review

Ask what the group accomplished, what remains unresolved, which costs or continuing effects still apply, and what each player wants to pursue. Check acquisitions, mirrored drawbacks, Item BU and pending rules changes together. Save the records and their versions so the next session begins from the world you actually created.

You have enough to run a game when the participants understand their characters, the situation offers useful choices, and the table can agree and record an attempt. The purpose of the tools is to support that conversation and the story that follows it.
Worked records and table references

The following constructions reproduce their ingredients so they can be used without a live catalogue. They are examples, not additional mandatory character choices. Acquisition costs use the reference anchors; execution stakes remain contextual.
Mira: a complete starting character

**Concept.** Mira grew up repairing canal boats. She wants to reopen the abandoned trade route and discover why the river no longer follows its old course. She knows the work of water better than court etiquette and needs companions who can help her reach the old locks.

rows: 6 remaining until a completed long rest refreshes it
Walking 30 ft per round; ordinary swim/climb 15 ft

blocks.text: Her practices use the full parent attribute. Prowess, Finesse and Fieldcraft are +3; Awareness, Reason and Influence +3; Knowledge +5; Mysticism, Communion and Intuition +6. Those are combined check bonuses, not numbers to which the same attribute and PB are added again. Saving throws are separate: +3 Physical, +3 Mental and +6 Magical. The chosen proficient Magical attribute supplies PB to its saving throw as well as its practices; further grants and direct modifiers follow their actual scope.

rows: Permission to change existing states/properties within owned domain access: reshape, redirect, combine, separate, transfer or stabilize
Grounded water is an eligible subject; no permission to control every grounded domain or abstract meaning of water
Permit eligible workings up to 30 ft; use actual target location and path
Permit d8 output in an appropriate damage/healing construction; no automatic number of dice or new behavior
Add PB to applicable Knowledge checks where that training is not already supplied

blocks.text: **River Caravan Upbringing** organizes Verb II, Water I and Knowledge proficiency: 16 BU of the existing ledger. It describes canal work, communal repairs and the habit of asking where a current will go. It does not add a second charge for those acquisitions.

**Guided Water, an effect.** References Verb II, Water I and Near Range. It permits guiding or reshaping existing grounded water that Mira can locate within 30 ft. Define the actual volume, route and opposition for the attempted use. It supplies neither an invisible-target lock nor unconditional control of every flow.

**River Hand, a capability.** Uses Guided Water to redirect streams or transfer water between vessels. Ordinary small tasks can need no roll or meaningful Cost. A surging canal may require resolution, more time, help or agreed consequences. Duration and upkeep are agreed for the actual working. The d8 acquisition can support a separately defined water impact; River Hand's description alone is not a healing power.

**Sample use.** Mira diverts a narrow stream from a worker's legs. The table agrees that reshaping the existing water is within access; the worker is visible and 20 ft away. They choose a Magical check under current conditions, DC 12, before commitment. With Magical proficiency her combined bonus is +6. A roll of 7 gives 13. The diversion succeeds with the pre-agreed restriction: she keeps directing this channel until the worker crosses. There is no second purchase of Water I and no automatic d8 damage.
A complete ordinary item

**Canal hook.** A Medium two-handed pole with a hook used to draw a rope closer or brace a light object. It has no extraordinary ingredient: Item BU 0, Load 2, final equipped requirement 2 slots. A carried spare still adds Load but uses no equipped slot. Its length gives no automatic Near Range permission for extraordinary workings.

Mira can carry and equip one hook: 2 of 55 Load and 2 of 6 equipped slots. Two hooks contribute 4 Load; equipping both requires 4 slots. Ordinary price and availability are setting decisions, not BU. A backpack organizes them without increasing capacity by default.

**Example authored augmentation.** “While this hook is equipped and braced on a stable support, add +2 to Prowess checks to hold a gate open.” Record a proposed Item BU price, such as 4, for review. The condition and check are exact; it neither increases Physical nor helps every attack. The hook's two slots and Load 2 remain unless another explicit rule changes them. The augmented hook is a different item record, not a free benefit in the ordinary hook above.
Read a creature: Canal Watcher

**Purpose.** A river spirit guards a spawning bed beside a damaged sluice. It wants a safe flow, not slaughter. It warns anyone disturbing the gate and can negotiate if someone demonstrates a workable diversion.

rows: 25 BU; 20 acquired/spent; 5 remaining; no mirror credit
Rank 1; attribute points 3; Physical 2, Mental 0, Magical 1
Physical +2; Mental +0; Magical +3 from the proficient attribute; no extra save-training grant
Maximum/current 13/13; unused short-rest allowance 7 if agreed rests apply
Small; walking 25 ft; ordinary swim/climb 13 ft
Ordinary sight and hearing; no granted sense through walls
None: Item BU 0; six equipment slots; carrying capacity 20 + 5 × 2 = 30

blocks.text: The baseline follows r = sqrt(25/25) = 1; attribute points ceil(3r) = 3; PB 1 + ceil(r) = 2; Vitality ceil(25/2) = 13. It uses the same fully stated Verb II, Water I, Near Range and d8 definitions as Mira, totaling 20 BU. It has no Knowledge proficiency purchase.

**Turn the Current.** A capability referencing Guided Water's Verb II, Water I and Near Range ingredients. Redirect or reshape existing located water within 30 ft. State the actual path, volume, recipients and opposition before resolving. This does not automatically move a creature against its will; contest or another agreed resolution can be needed.

**Water Impact.** Uses those ingredients and d8 output to drive existing water into one located target within 30 ft. **Example normal expression:** 1d8 Magical Water damage, projected through the actual path. At this table it uses an attack check with Magical training, +3, against the target's DC; it does not also demand a save by default. Appraise changed volume, recipients, timing or effort separately. This sample expression grants no healing, resistance or extra actions.

**Behavior and tells.** The Watcher points toward the spawning bed before attacking. It prefers turning the current to injuring people. It retreats or talks when the threat to the bed ends. A dry bank deprives it of useful existing water; its unused BU does not grant water creation, armor or teleportation.

In the digital creature editor, practice-allocation slices may be recorded as Physical Prowess 2/Finesse 0/Fieldcraft 0; Magical Mysticism 1/Communion 0/Intuition 0; Mental all 0. Those allocations satisfy its base ledger; the displayed checks still use the relevant full current attribute and applicable training, as listed above.
Progress beyond level 21

Progression does not stop at level 20. Retain the published cumulative threshold at level 21, 286 BU. After that, add 10 each level and the subsequent four-level bracket spikes: +24 at level 25, +28 at 29, +32 at 33, continuing in that pattern. These are additions to the ordinary +10 at those levels. PB still follows 2 + floor((level - 1)/4).
Do not add a spike again to an already cumulative table value. Active PB and Vitality modifiers can change the resolved sheet.
Mirror credit without erasing the drawback

**Example, not a mandatory build.** A level 1 character has 25 BU and spends 27 on positive acquisitions. An accepted eligible personal drawback supplies 2 credit, giving 25 net spent and 2 actual used debt. The level 1 debt ceiling is 4. The positive build is also below the next-level creation ceiling of 35. Review the drawback's actual rule and obtain the DM's agreement to exceed the ordinary allowance.

Having a ceiling of 4 does not mean the character automatically receives 4 credit. A character spending 23 has 2 ordinary BU remaining, even if the sheet also shows potential mirror headroom. A character proposing 31 positive BU with only 2 valid credit remains 29 net spent: another 4 is not covered merely because a ceiling exists. Overflow still needs explicit agreement and must respect both applicable limits.

Compatible pairs are Add/Subtract, Multiply/Divide, Minimum/Maximum and Grant/Revoke. Set To has no automatic opposite. A personal drawback that revokes flight remains on that person; separately proposing flight for an ally does not repay or suppress it. A narrow condition or non-mirrorable rule must be respected.
At the table: a quick reference

items: State an intent. Confirm ordinary circumstances and extraordinary access.
Locate the target or establish an authored alternative. Declare actual reach, recipients, output and duration.
Agree uncertainty, stakes, Cost and its timing. Revise the attempt if needed.
Resolve the chosen check, contest, clash, attack or save; apply bias and modifiers once.
Record changed positions, current Vitality, movement used, reactions, consequences and ongoing requirements.

rows: d20 + current attribute + applicable training + modifiers
PB / twice PB where actually granted
Cancel opposing stacks; N net stacks means N + 1 dice, keep appropriate extreme
One independent slot per round; valid trigger, immediate Complexity 0-1, self/touch or one target
One round allowance; split among tracks/reactions as the situation permits
One upkeep track per maintained capability; requirements of several capabilities accumulate
Matching resistance half rounded up; vulnerability double; immunity zero
Rescue promptly; stabilization stops dying but does not heal or wake
Finite allowance ceil(max Vitality/2); consume actual healing, carry unused recovery
Agreed overnight recovery; normally full healing, refresh short-rest allowance
Count acquisitions once; character BU, Item BU and execution Cost remain separate

blocks.text: Glossary
**Acquisition:** an owned occurrence of a primitive, recorded in its ledger. References to it in several compositions are not extra purchases.
**Attribute:** Physical, Mental or Magical; use its current numerical value directly.
**BU, Build Units:** the acquisition measure. It is not automatically money, a spell resource or an encounter difficulty rating.
**Capability:** a working or talent organized from actual primitives, effects and readable rules.
**Clash:** a timing resolution when opposing intents meet; distinct from a contest of effort.
**Complexity:** the dependencies of an action, used in placing it in the shared rhythm; distinct from power or Strain.
**Consequence:** an actual change with a cause, applicable timing and ending/recovery terms.
**Cost:** the agreed pressure or consequence of an attempted execution; may be mechanical, restrictive, environmental or narrative.
**Council:** the coordination/continuation point at the beginning of a shared round.
**DC:** a difficulty target; a character's selected-attribute DC is distinct from their three saving throws.
**Domain:** the subject that an extraordinary permission can affect.
**Effect:** a reusable grouping of ingredients or outcomes; it is not an automatic new purchase.
**Heritage:** Lineage, Upbringing or Manifest: a narrative organization of actual acquired content.
**Intent:** the outcome an actor wants, stated before the resolution procedure is chosen.
**Item BU:** the separate acquisition accounting for equipment mechanics.
**Load:** carried burden; distinct from equipped slots, Item BU and ordinary value.
**Mirror:** an eligible reversed rule with actual scope and an accepted drawback; not an unrestricted cancellation trick.
**PB:** proficiency bonus. Apply applicable training once; expertise uses twice PB when granted.
**Practice:** an approach to a check associated with an attribute; ordinary attempts do not require training.
**Primitive:** a reusable permission or rule, with its own recipients, conditions and accounting.
**Reaction:** an immediate eligible response through an available independent slot and actual trigger.
**Strain:** contextual appraisal of how an attempt pushes the actor and situation, graded 0-6 as guidance.
**Structure:** the permitted arrangement of a working; it supplies no unrelated domain or verb access.
**Template / play copy:** a reusable creature definition / one independent creature's state in play.
**Track:** Fast, Measured or Heavy resolution timing in a shared round.
**Upkeep:** an agreed ongoing requirement of a maintained working; not necessarily damage.
**Verb:** the kind of change an extraordinary permission allows.
**Vitality:** current capacity to remain in action; its maximum and current value are separate.

Suggested attribution: “Based on SwordWeave v0.1 alpha by Marius Ion, swordweave.quest, licensed CC BY 4.0. Changes: [describe your changes].” The bracketed phrase is an instruction to reusers, not a missing credit in this book.

The SwordWeave name, wordmark and brand identity identify the project; this notice grants no trademark or endorsement rights. title: System Reference Document
subtitle: The open construction and play framework.
description: A precise reference for the rules, 29 primitive families, construction procedures and compatible creation.

blocks.text: Rules edition: **v0.1 alpha** · 12 October 2026 · Free open reference.

This document states the complete construction and play framework, including the base primitive families, characters, effects, capabilities, heritages, items, creatures and encounter procedures. It is a reference for play and compatible creation. The PHB teaches these procedures; the GM Guide demonstrates applying them. No fixed class system or exhaustive bestiary is required. One explicitly marked Vitality upkeep rule remains pending in this alpha.
Core procedure
Participants and intent

Players portray their characters. The Dungeon Master or Game Master describes the world, portrays other participants and adjudicates outcomes with the table. The group agrees the intended setting, starting budget and relevant expectations before play.
An intent states the result an actor wants. Before commitment, establish:

items: The intended result.
Applicable ordinary circumstances and extraordinary access.
Scope, targets, reach, output, timing and persistence.
Stakes, cost and consequences.
Resolution procedure.

blocks.text: The actor can accept, narrow or revise the attempt. Resolve uncertainty when needed, apply the agreed result and consequences, then continue from the changed situation.
Rule of Cool

**Core rule.** Give exciting ideas a chance. Discuss what makes the attempt possible, what it risks and how it will resolve. Use the actual situation to support a coherent, engaging and cinematic scene.

The table can agree an exception or variation. State its scope and consequences explicitly. An exceptional outcome does not silently grant unrelated permanent permissions or erase an existing consequence.
Rules and examples

**Core rule** identifies the framework. **Default** identifies the supplied procedure. **Authored rule** identifies a specific component's permission, condition, limit or exception. **Optional guidance** identifies a treatment the table may select. **Example** illustrates a case. **App note** explains a digital operation.
Use the agreed procedure for the actual situation. Published examples are not universal prices or consequences.
Character foundation and construction
Attributes and practices

**Default.** Base Physical, Mental and Magical total 10; each is from -1 to +5. Relevant primitives can modify the resulting values. Use current numerical attribute values directly rather than converting them into another modifier scale.

Ordinary attempts do not require training. Relevant full attribute applies to a practice check. Training adds PB where applicable; expertise uses twice PB where granted. Grants that establish the same training do not automatically add PB repeatedly. An explicit numerical bonus follows its own authored rule.
Build Units and components
BU pays for acquisition of reusable primitives. A default level 1 foundation has 25 BU. Item BU is separate. Agree custom or higher-level starting budgets with the DM.

A primitive establishes a reusable permission or rule. Effects group ingredients or outcomes; capabilities organize complete workings. Lineage, upbringing and manifest organize ancestry, experience and current expression. Their names do not grant mechanics beyond their stated content.

A character foundation requires owned positive verb and domain access in the character build; items do not satisfy this requirement. Missing range and output categories receive the zero-BU Touch and 1d4 baselines.

Reusing an owned primitive in another composition does not repurchase it. Deliberately acquiring additional occurrences, acquiring new ingredients and accepting permitted mirrored drawbacks require their own accounting.
Authored prices and stacking
Library/builder prices and tiers are guidance. Authors select BU prices; the DM may accept them or request adjustments. Scope, conditions, restrictions and stacking can affect the price.

Applicable contributions stack by default unless the authored stacking rules state otherwise. Enforce conditions, uniqueness and scope. Permission grants, numerical contributions and roll behavior are distinct; a counter is not automatically a static +1.
Construction reference
Component records

**Authored rule.** Record the name, readable rule, actual ingredients, recipients/targets, applicable conditions, operations and values, stacking/uniqueness restrictions and relevant ending conditions. State a proposed BU price for an acquisition. A label or descriptive name grants only the rules actually recorded.

A primitive may grant permission, contribute a numerical change or define a descriptive rule. An effect groups related ingredients or outcomes. A capability organizes a working or talent and may reference effects and primitives. Lineage, Upbringing and Manifest organize character heritage. Items carry their own ingredients and accounting. These containers do not automatically create additional acquisitions or permission grants.

Reusing the same acquired primitive in several compositions does not repurchase it. Deliberately acquired additional occurrences follow their authored rules and acquisition costs. Resolve overlapping references against the actual acquisitions rather than treating every appearance as another free contribution.
Find the base definitions

The primitive reference below reproduces the principal 29 families, bound access-tier meanings, reach/output ladders and core grant examples. Finished catalogue options and forks are supplementary. A family label alone is not a permission; read the actual subject, recipient, conditions and scope.
Construct an effect or capability

items: Describe the intended result.
Identify the ordinary circumstances and extraordinary access supporting it.
Select acquired primitives and, where useful, related effects.
Specify actual grants/changes and applicable recipients, conditions, stacking and limits.
Describe the normal use or trigger and any duration/continuation requirements.
Identify which details are fixed by the construction and which are appraised for each attempted use.
Review the definition and acquisition accounting with the table; test contrasting uses.

blocks.text: A capability need not contain a separately named effect. Neither container grants mechanics absent from its actual ingredients or descriptive rules. A new arrangement of existing purchases is not itself a new purchase of those ingredients.
Construct a heritage or character

For a heritage, choose Lineage, Upbringing or Manifest according to its narrative purpose. Describe the heritage, select actual ingredients/capabilities, identify acquisitions and record any genuine drawbacks. Review the resulting scope and suggested cost. A descriptive history need not grant mechanical benefits.

For a character, agree the starting budget/level, allocate base attributes, choose the proficient attribute and practice training, establish owned positive verb/domain access, acquire the chosen ingredients, organize heritage/capabilities, then resolve the final sheet. Keep Item BU and equipment accounting separate. Check derived formulas, active modifiers and consequences. A player may use an existing creation, adapt it or author one.

**Checked example.** Mira's upbringing organizes Verb II (8), Water domain I (4) and Knowledge proficiency (4): 16 BU. Near Range (4) and d8 (4) bring her total to 24/25 BU. Organizing Water/Verb/Near in Guided Water and River Hand does not change that acquisition total. Her attribute allocation and derived values appear in the PHB character example.
Construct creatures and encounters

**Default creature foundation - current builder reference.** Choose a positive base creature budget B. Rank r = sqrt(B / 25); base attribute points = ceil(3r); PB = 1 + ceil(r); baseline Vitality = max(1, ceil(B / 2)). Allocate the available nonnegative attribute points, select the proficient attribute and distribute practice slices consistently with the practice-allocation rules. Authored modifiers and an explicit agreed Vitality baseline can change the resolved sheet. These are creature baselines, not the player character's starting allocation or Vitality formula.

Describe the creature's encounter purpose, senses, movement and behavior. Select and review actual primitives, effects, capabilities, heritages or items that support its abilities. Resolve active modifiers, conditions, practices, output and Vitality. Show base budget, acquired/spent creature BU, permitted mirror credit and remaining creature BU separately; equipment contributes separate Item BU. Shared ingredients are accounted against their acquisitions rather than repeatedly charged through containers. A higher maximum does not automatically restore current Vitality.

**Worked construction.** A 25-BU Canal Watcher has r = 1, three base attribute points, PB 2 and baseline Vitality 13. Allocate Physical 2, Mental 0 and Magical 1. Verb II (8), Water domain I (4), Near Range (4) and d8 (4) spend 20 creature BU, leaving 5; this example has no mirror credit and no equipment. Its water manipulation is appraised through the recorded permissions. A title such as “guardian” grants no armor, extra actions or area attack.

For an encounter, record the objective/situation, party BU and separate Party Item BU, any known party size, the chosen creatures and quantities. Multiply chosen base creature budgets and resolved Item BU by quantity. Compare totals, counts and concentration of budget where those facts are available. Mirror credit is not another creature's budget. Spent/remaining creature BU describes a build; encounter appraisal uses its chosen base budget.

**Worked appraisal.** Two Canal Watchers contribute 2 × 25 = 50 enemy creature BU and 0 enemy Item BU. A party with 50 Party BU and 8 Party Item BU has a combined 58; the enemy combined total is 50. Enemy minus party is -8, and the enemy/party ratio is 50/58. If party size is two, counts match; each Watcher contains half the enemy creature budget. None of these facts establishes a difficulty rating.

Comparable BU does not promise comparable difficulty. Objectives, terrain, information, control, area effects, support, burst damage and how the table applies the rules affect play. Manual party totals are sufficient; linked sheets are optional budget references. Run the encounter with the shared Council → Fast → Measured → Heavy rhythm, current creature state and agreed consequences.

**App note.** Catalogue templates, immutable versions, independent play copies and encounter runs organize digital reuse and tracking. Publication links add convenience; offline construction requires the actual relevant definitions. Starting a digital run creates private play copies; choosing or previewing a template does not modify another user's creature or character.
Resolution
Progression and mirrored acquisitions

**Default.** Acquisition BU, Item BU and execution Cost are separate. Unspent BU may acquire or invent ingredients during play with table agreement. Spending acquisition budget does not undo progression. The DM/table establishes rewards and pacing; there is no compulsory XP or per-session award schedule.
The cumulative table includes bracket spikes. Add them only through the progression procedure, never again to a listed cumulative threshold. Apply active PB/Vitality modifiers after these baselines.

Compatible operations can be mirrored within their actual scope and access: Add ↔ Subtract; Multiply ↔ Divide; Minimum ↔ Maximum; Grant ↔ Revoke. Set To has no automatic opposite. Descriptive reversals require a coherent agreed meaning. An accepted personal drawback remains in effect and in the acquisition accounting even when a separate action proposes another direction.

The default debt ceiling is 4 × ceil(level / 4): 4 at levels 1-4, 8 at 5-8, 12 at 9-12, and onward. Ordinary remaining BU, available drawback credit and actual used debt are distinct. Creation fills ordinary budget, then eligible credit, then any remaining overflow; exceeding the ordinary allowance requires DM agreement and cannot exceed the next-level creation ceiling or permitted drawback debt. Later sheet warnings are app behavior, not permission to ignore those agreed constraints.
Checks and formulas

**Default attack:** d20 + relevant current attribute + applicable training + attack modifiers versus the target's DC. Meet or beat the DC to hit, then resolve damage/effect separately. A miss does not apply the hit's damage unless specifically stated.

**Default save:** d20 + relevant current attribute + applicable saving-throw training + save modifiers versus the user's DC. Select the Physical, Mental or Magical save according to the capability/source and its actual resolution. The chosen proficient attribute grants PB to its own save; others require an actual grant to gain that training. Repeated grants of the same training do not add PB repeatedly. Success/failure follows the working's stated or agreed outcome. An attack and a save are not both required by default.
**Default check:** d20 + relevant current attribute + applicable training + applicable modifiers. Meet or beat the agreed DC. A displayed combined bonus is added once.

rows: 5 + current PB + chosen eligible current modified attribute + direct DC modifiers
(10 + current PB) × level, then active maximum-Vitality rules

blocks.text: One selected-attribute DC is distinct from Physical, Mental and Magical saving throws. An attack and a saving throw are different resolution methods; a working does not require both by default.

Use applicable combined bonuses once. Check/roll result floors, ceilings and fixed results apply at their authored scope, distinct from attribute/stat bounds. No automatic natural-20 success, natural-1 failure or critical-damage multiplier is imported; an authored rule or agreed table variation can establish its own effect.
Ordinary rounding is upward. The explicit floor in the PB formula specifies its own operation. Authored result limits and other exceptions state their own scope.
Advantage and disadvantage
**Default.** Apply authored stacking restrictions, then cancel opposing advantage/disadvantage stacks one-for-one. Let N be the absolute remaining count.

items: Net advantage: roll N + 1 resolution dice; keep the highest.
Net disadvantage: roll N + 1 resolution dice; keep the lowest.
Zero net bias: roll one resolution die.

blocks.text: **Example.** Two advantages and one disadvantage leave one advantage: 2d20, highest. Two advantages with no opposing source: 3d20, highest. The applicable static bonus is then added once.
Scope and targeting
Access and use

Verb and domain permissions determine eligible changes and subjects. Range and output permissions determine access to reach and die types. Selected dice count, area, targets, duration and other declared scaling can increase pressure without each requiring another purchase by default. Extra behaviors can require additional access.
Sensory location

**Default.** Targeting a specific creature or object requires locating it through an applicable sense. Ordinary vision, granted blindsight, tremorsense or another suitable sensory permission can provide that location.
Without it, an actor can propose targeting a known spot or area and resolve uncertainty at the table. A chosen area does not guarantee a desired creature is present.

**Authored rule.** A working such as scrying, widespread weather influence or “any qualifying target within range” can establish a different targeting method. Range alone does not grant information or override the working's targeting requirements.
Range permissions

Default reference maximums are Near 30 ft, Far 60 ft and Very Far 120 ft. Extreme permits continuous reach up to approximately three miles, including nearer targets. The table can agree broader scope, including Extreme beyond three miles, with appropriate access and consequences. These permissions do not reveal targets or remove sensory/targeting requirements.
Combat and movement
Shared rhythm

Council coordinates intent. Fast resolves Complexity 0-1, Measured resolves 2-3 and Heavy resolves 4+. Complexity describes timing dependencies rather than damage or power. There is no default initiative roll.

One independent Reaction Slot resets at Council. A default reaction has a valid trigger, immediate Complexity 0-1 and self/touch or a single-target scope. Relevant access and actual timing still apply.

Describe one coherent Main Intent and establish dependent actions. A Reaction Clash resolves colliding opposing intents within a track when timing matters: d20 + relevant attribute + applicable training/modifiers; higher acts first. On a tie the GM resolves simultaneously or follows the stronger fictional position. An Active Contest resolves a direct struggle using each side's relevant approach; higher wins the immediate struggle. Use combined practice totals once. Losing a clash does not automatically erase the Main Intent; pivot when changed circumstances require it.
For a valid reaction, pause the triggering event, resolve the response, then continue. It may occur before or after the Main Intent and does not automatically cancel its trigger.
Movement allowance

**Default.** Speed is ordinary movement available across the whole round. Spend some or all and divide it among tracks and valid reactions. It can accompany an intent or be used independently where the situation permits. Spending a Reaction Slot does not provide a new movement allowance.
Moving farther requires appropriate speed access or an agreed cost/consequence. Actual routes, hazards, interference and the Rule of Cool guide the ruling.
**Example.** Speed 30 ft permits 10 ft during Fast and 20 ft during Heavy. Additional movement requires a further permission or table agreement.
Swimming/climbing use half base speed rounded up. Apply authored changes; flight and burrowing require granted access.
Surprise

**Optional guidance.** There is no universal surprise mechanic. An ambush can justify the prepared side completing one round before surprised participants respond. Circumstances or an agreed d20 check can change this treatment.
Costs and persistence
Contextual consequences

Strain describes how an attempt pushes the actor and situation. Agree costs and their timing before commitment. Costs can be Vitality, resources, numerical penalties, restrictions, temporary loss of access, tasks, environmental effects or narrative consequences; combinations and negligible costs are possible.

Maintaining a working generally spreads pressure out or lowers upfront demand compared with forcing an increased expression in one round. There is no universal discount or conversion into damage. Specify the continuation requirements and the duration/ending of any consequence.

The 0-6 Strain grades guide appraisal: effortless, light effort, noticeable strain, heavy burden, dangerous instability, critical risk and catastrophic consequence. They are not automatic bills or fixed success probabilities. Consider scale, impact, dependencies/complexity, environment, opposition and urgency. Declared dice count, area, targets or duration can add pressure without each requiring another purchase by default; new behaviors may require additional access.

**Optional guidance.** Let B be the minimum evaluated composition and A the selected evaluated use. ΔCV = A - B; total CV = B + ΔCV = A. With B = 12 and A = 30, increase is 18 and total is 30. These illustrate arithmetic, not a universal spell price. CV is neither a roll bonus nor acquisition BU paid again, and numerical scaling cannot capture every contextual demand.

**Core rule.** A consequence records its cause, actual change, timing/trigger and ending/recovery terms. Names do not import universal numerical packages. Agree when Cost applies and what failure means; interruption has no universal refund.
Upkeep

Track, duration and upkeep are separate properties. A maintained capability has one upkeep track even when it contains multiple effects. Several capabilities can be maintained; their agreed requirements accumulate. Continuing and ending follow the working's actual conditions.

Agree an explicit continuation point in the shared round, such as Council. A recurring 4-Vitality requirement can be due again next round; a loss of access follows its own duration/ending condition. Interference needs actual access, position, timing and resolution. A hit alone is not a universal interruption. An actor unable to perform a required task cannot continue it. Instant actions cannot be interrupted retroactively after resolution; resulting ongoing effects may be separately disrupted through appropriate access.

**Alpha rule pending - damage-triggered Vitality upkeep.** Additional repayment triggered by incoming damage, including threshold and counter/reset/excess handling, is undecided. This edition does not impose that numerical scheme. Agree any temporary table treatment explicitly. Ordinary continuation requirements remain usable; do not apply the unresolved scheme to non-Vitality upkeep.
Recovery and equipment
Agreed rests

A short rest is a short pause, perhaps 15 or 30 minutes. A long rest is overnight sleep or equivalent recovery, not necessarily eight hours. DM and players agree whether their effects apply; elapsed time never applies recovery automatically.

**Default short rest.** Allow recovery equal to half maximum Vitality, rounded up, between completed long rests. Only actual Vitality restored consumes the allowance. Unused recovery carries into subsequent short rests; it cannot heal above maximum.

**Default long rest.** Restore to maximum and refresh the short-rest allowance. The table can agree partial healing after a completed long rest. Long-rest healing is independent of the short-rest allowance. Injuries and other lasting consequences use their stated recovery requirements.
**Example.** Maximum 13 gives allowance 7. At 10/13, heal 3; 4 remains for later short rests. A completed long rest refreshes that allowance.
Stabilization and healing

At zero Vitality, the character collapses, unconscious and incapacitated. Collapse uses a contextual rescue countdown; roughly a minute is guidance, not ten guaranteed safe rounds. Dedicate an action track to Fieldcraft stabilization or suitable owned primitives, with agreed access, resolution and Cost; no universal stabilization DC is prescribed. Success halts the countdown without granting Vitality or consciousness. Healing above zero ends the dying state and restores consciousness unless another consequence prevents it. A stabilized character can recover through assisted rest; active dying requires rescue first.
Damage and lethal thresholds

Physical, Magical and Psychic are execution sources; domains identify the output's nature. Mental is an attribute. Read actual source/domain scope: resistance halves matching damage rounded up, vulnerability doubles it, immunity negates covered damage. Multiple resistances do not quarter damage by default. Applicable resistance/vulnerability on an instance cancel. Damage immunity alone does not negate every associated condition.

Mixed output needs an explicit source/domain breakdown and identification of split versus separate instances. Apply final post-defense damage as Vitality loss. Healing is capped by current maximum; increasing maximum alone does not heal.
**Examples.** Nine Magical Fire becomes 5 under matching resistance, 18 under vulnerability or 9 with both. Six Physical Fire + eight Magical Fire totals 10 under Magical-only resistance (6 + 4).

One execution dealing at least twice maximum Vitality, or taking current Vitality to -maximum Vitality, can cause immediate death under the massive-damage rule. Establish lethal stakes beforehand. Use current Vitality before the hit and final post-defense damage rather than a sheet's stored zero clamp. Maximum 13/current 4/final damage 17 reaches -13; final damage 26 independently reaches twice maximum. The collapse clock is distinct from an outright lethal result.
Equipped slots

**Default.** Six universal equipment slots. An ordinary equipped item occupies one; a two-handed item occupies two. A higher authored requirement can represent unusual gear, and primitives can extend available slots. Size alone does not multiply the final requirement.

Load, Item BU and equipped slots are distinct measures. Equipped items still contribute carried Load. A small character's unusually large sword may be permitted with an explicit three/four-slot requirement or another agreed consequence.
Load and delivery paths

Capacity = size base + 5 × current Physical + applicable bonuses. Load above capacity is encumbered; the GM/table determines penalties and complications. Equipped items still count toward carried Load. Explicit authored Load rules can change an item's contribution. A backpack organizes contents without automatically adding capacity.
One pouch holds up to 1,000 tiny objects and contributes 1 Load. Item BU, ordinary value and Load remain independent.

Projected vectors travel through intervening space. Minor obstruction imposes -2 accuracy; standard half cover -4; total cover blocks the trajectory. Evaluate actual angle/path. Direct manifestation appears at a target and ignores those intervening projected-cover penalties, but still requires sensory location or an authored targeting method. Cover does not automatically grant knowledge of a hidden target.
Reference conventions and rule boundaries

This extended reference supplies readable record formats, explicit calculations and procedures for compatible SwordWeave creation. It supplements the principal primitive families and play rules in this SRD. It does not require a platform account, a particular database, a fixed class list or a separate monster book. Keep the actual definitions needed for play with the record; a name, image or unavailable link cannot substitute for an ingredient's rule.

**Core rule.** The table establishes an intended result, checks ordinary circumstances and extraordinary access, agrees the actual scope and stakes, chooses the appropriate resolution, then carries the result forward. Permission to propose an outcome and success at accomplishing it are different facts. Ordinary actions remain possible without purchasing a primitive for every task.

**Default** means the supplied procedure unless the table agrees a variation. **Authored rule** means a particular component's recorded permission, operation, condition, restriction or exception. **Optional guidance** means a tool the group may choose. **Example** means the stated construction or situation, including its example prices. **App note** describes digital organization or calculation; it does not add a tabletop prerequisite.
Three records to keep distinct

rows: What is the rule or construction?
A bound Water permission; a capability's ingredients; an item's equipped requirement
Which occurrence does this actor own, and how was it counted?
One Water I acquisition for 4 BU; a separately purchased permitted occurrence
What is true of this actor or scene now?
Current Vitality; movement already used; a maintained channel; an injury

blocks.text: A new capability can organize existing acquisitions without changing the acquisition ledger. Using that capability can change state without editing its definition. Editing a definition can change the resolved sheet without automatically healing the actor or clearing a consequence. Track the relationship explicitly when several people use the same template.

**Example.** The definition of Guided Water references Verb II, Water I and Near. Mira owns one acquisition of each. She presently maintains one channel beside a stair. Adding another capability that references the same three acquisitions neither buys them again nor creates another channel already in the world. A second actual channel requires a new attempted use and appraisal of its scope and requirements.
Complete does not mean automated

A complete record lets people decide what qualifies, what changes and what ends. Descriptive rules can be complete without becoming a static sheet number. A narrative obligation may identify a person, deadline and consequence rather than an arithmetic modifier. A sensory permission may describe information and barriers rather than supply an attack bonus.

When a rule is ambiguous, clarify its intended meaning with the author and table. Do not replace missing terms with a familiar package from another game. A condition named stunned, blessed or invisible grants only its stated consequences. A creature labeled boss has only its actual economy. A heritage title grants only its actual content.
What compatibility requires

A compatible creation should identify which SwordWeave defaults it uses and which rules it changes. It should retain intelligible acquisition accounting, actual permissions and scopes, the distinction between character and item budgets, and the agreed resolution procedure. A campaign may choose different budgets, consequences or optional tools without concealing those changes as unchanged defaults.

A construction's BU figure does not establish approval in every campaign. Its author proposes a price; the table reviews the actual content and can accept or revise it. Suggested catalogue anchors are reference points, not universal tariffs guaranteeing equivalence between every similarly priced rule.
Readable construction record formats

These formats specify the information people need to use a construction. They are not API payloads or mandatory software field names. Combine fields into readable paragraphs where convenient. Omit genuinely irrelevant details; explicitly settle details that affect the intended use. A paper label such as Water acquisition A can identify a purchase just as well as a digital identifier.

It is a numerical practice-check contribution, not a Physical increase. Its recipient is its owner, not everyone using their rope. The example proposes 4 BU. Its authored rule must settle any deliberate additional occurrence before that occurrence is used; two references to the first acquisition are not two qualifying purchases.

blocks.text: An effect need not introduce a separate execution or upkeep requirement. If it is used inside a maintained capability, the capability's actual continuation governs that use. If the author intends an independently maintained working, identify it as such rather than allowing the nesting diagram to decide.

**Example effect.** Guided Water organizes Verb II, grounded Water I and Near. It supports guiding or reshaping existing located water within 30 ft. The attempted volume, route, opposition and continuation are appraised in use. It does not create water, grant Life access or automatically move every creature standing in the water.

Actor and encounter record formats

An actor record combines a foundation, acquisitions, resolved values and current state. An encounter record organizes several such actors and a situation. Neither record grants new permissions merely by naming them.

During a run add independent actor state, round/phase, intent and resolution markers, objective changes and meaningful events. Visibility settings and digital ownership are platform properties, not encounter difficulty or character permissions.
Acquisitions, occurrences and dependency accounting
Count ownership before counting appearances

An acquisition is one owned occurrence counted in the appropriate ledger. A reference says that a construction uses an acquisition or definition. A nested appearance says where that reference can be found. Those are different relationships. The same acquisition can support several compositions without being charged again or supplying several copies of its numerical contribution to one check.

Identify shared ingredients when reading a bundled heritage or capability. If two capabilities both reference Water acquisition A, their container totals can each display Water's cost as composition information. Adding those displayed totals is not automatically the character's acquisition total. Resolve the actor's ledger against actual owned occurrences.

Deliberately purchasing additional occurrences is a different choice. Record quantity, cost and the actual stacking or uniqueness rules. A second purchase is not automatically useful: a unique training state or nonstacking defense may be unchanged. Owning several rules also does not automatically grant several Main Intents.
A complete reusable ledger
**Example.** An actor owns these five acquisitions. The bound access definitions below reproduce everything needed for the example; they are not a fixed class package.

rows: Verb II: change eligible existing states or properties by reshaping, redirecting, combining, separating, transferring or stabilizing
Water I: grounded existing water is an eligible subject; no grant of all grounded domains
Near: eligible reach up to 30 ft with actual targeting and delivery requirements
d8 output: this die type is available for an appropriate damage/healing construction; no automatic behavior or dice count
Knowledge proficiency: supply PB training where not already supplied

blocks.text: Guided Water references V-A, W-A and R-A. River Hand uses Guided Water. Canal Impact references those same three acquisitions plus D-A. River Caravan Upbringing organizes V-A, W-A and K-A. All four constructions can be recorded without a second charge for their overlapping ingredients. The actor's positive ledger stays 24 BU.

If the actor uses River Hand to divert water and Canal Impact later to strike, both uses rely on the same ownership. Each actual attempt still has its own timing, scope, resolution and consequences. The names do not create simultaneous free outputs. If a rule instead explicitly consumes a resource on each use, track that authored resource separately from the acquisition.
Acquisition and active contribution are separate

A condition can make a purchased rule inactive without refunding its price. An unequipped item can remain owned and carried without supplying its equipped-only bonus. An accepted drawback can remain in the ledger while its condition is presently absent; its real eligible scope still matters when reviewing credit.

Likewise, suppressing a rule through a consequence changes availability, not ownership. If Water reshaping is unavailable until a stated task, the character does not silently receive its BU back. A build edit that removes a purchase needs table agreement about replacement, accounting and existing state.
Ingredient availability and adopted versions

A readable offline record should reproduce the relevant ingredient definitions or include an accessible reference copy. Record the adopted edition when changing versions could change mechanics. A newer published definition does not automatically alter everyone's current character, template or run.

**App note.** Digital compositions can reference pinned definitions and resolve their dependencies through the platform. A visible container does not grant access to another person's private ingredients. Availability and ownership are checked through existing permissions. If a preparation contains an inaccessible reference, treat its unresolved information as unknown rather than displaying private details or pretending its budget is zero.

For paper play, the same principle is practical rather than technical: make the actual approved rules available to the group. A missing page or inaccessible link prevents reproducible appraisal until the definition is supplied or replaced. This is not a requirement to obtain a digital account.
Quantity belongs to a real occurrence

State what quantity counts. Three creatures are three actors. Three hooks are three physical items. Two permitted numerical acquisitions can supply two contributions if their actual rules allow it. Three references to one hook are not three hooks; three references to one Steady Hands acquisition are not three bonuses.

Multiplying quantity does not automatically multiply every other property. Two creatures have independent Vitality and reactions, not one creature with double its maximum. Carrying two hooks multiplies Load, but only actually equipped items use slots. Repeating a training grant establishes the same trained state unless a separately authored rule specifies a different contribution.
Numerical operations, grants and scope
Operation meanings

Choose the quantity before choosing the operation. An operation on an attribute, a practice bonus, a selected die, a final result or maximum Vitality can produce very different outcomes. Read the rule's actual stage and scope.

Decrease it by the stated amount
Subtract 2 from a specified attack bonus

Multiply covered damage by 2 for vulnerability

Halve covered damage, rounded up, for resistance

A stated check result cannot be below 10

blocks.text: Ordinary rounding is upward where a calculation needs an integer. A formula that explicitly says floor retains that operation. A rule may establish its own particular exception. Division by zero is not a meaningful numerical rule; choose valid parameters and state their use.

Some operations interact. Adding 2 then multiplying by 2 differs from multiplying by 2 then adding 2. The framework does not turn unspecified order in an ambiguous creation into a new universal tabletop hierarchy. Define the intended quantity and interaction, show a before/after calculation and settle conflicts before relying on them. Preserve explicit special procedures, such as damage-defense cancellation and training upgrades, rather than replacing them with raw arithmetic.

**App note.** A digital resolver uses its supported operation order and metric scope. Authoring a modifier that produces a number in the app does not resolve unclear tabletop prose. Keep the human-readable rule and intended example consistent with its digital representation. If they differ, review the construction rather than treating a storage detail as a new core rule.
Grants are not always additions

Permission, training, state and bias grants require their stated interpretation. Granting Water access does not add Water's tier number to a roll. Granting flight establishes its actual movement permission; its speed and conditions still need definition. Granting proficiency upgrades applicable training rather than adding PB every time the same word appears.

For a practice, the current full parent attribute is the baseline contribution. Applicable proficiency supplies one PB. Eligible expertise brings training to twice PB. An expertise record should establish or identify the required proficiency; a bare ambiguous label is not a way to purchase repeated PB. Separate explicit numerical bonuses follow their own scope and stacking rules.

**Example.** At PB 2 and Mental 3, untrained Knowledge is +3. A valid proficiency grant makes it +5. A second proficiency grant leaves the training component at +2, so the total remains +5. Eligible expertise gives a +4 training component and a +7 total. An independently qualifying explicit +1 Knowledge bonus brings that check to +8; it does not become another proficiency state.

Saving-throw training is separate from practice training. The chosen proficient attribute supplies PB to its own practices and saving throw. Knowledge proficiency does not by itself train the Mental save. A Defensive Save Upgrade can grant training to its stated saving-throw scope without increasing Reason or Influence.

A projected support field can supply a stated ally bonus without transferring permanent ownership of its ingredients to those allies.
Provenance of a contribution

For a changed value, a useful breakdown identifies baseline, actual active source, recipient, condition, operation and result. Provenance explains why the value applies; it does not create an additional benefit.

**Example.** Torren's qualifying rope Finesse begins with Physical 5 and trained PB 2: +7. His owned Steady Hands supplies +2 while both hands are free. An agreed trembling-hands consequence subtracts 2 from delicate hand work until care and an agreed short rest. If both qualify, +7 +2 -2 = +7. The numerical cancellation does not end the consequence. If one hand is occupied, Steady Hands does not qualify, so the same injured check is +5.
Record the injury separately from the acquisition. Referencing Steady Hands through an upbringing and a capability is two provenance paths to one acquired rule, not an excuse to add its +2 twice.
Conditions, stacking and rule interactions
Define conditions that can be answered

A condition states when a rule applies. It can concern actor, target, scene, equipment, timing or a prior event. Identify the subject and enough detail for the table to answer. Avoid an undefined adjective doing the work of several different facts.

rows: Example of a settled authored condition
Within 10 ft of an open body of water large enough to immerse a hand
After securing both anchors, until either anchor is moved
Against a target located through this stated sense in an unlit area
While equipped, firmly anchored and applying force through the hook
Until the stated care and recovery condition, rather than any Vitality restoration

blocks.text: These replacements are examples, not mandatory definitions of those words. If the author intends a broader or narrower condition, write that condition. A restrictive condition can affect the proposed price, but no fixed percentage discount is implied.
Conditions do not import recipients or triggers

“While an ally falls” can qualify an actor's rule without establishing who can perceive the fall, whether they have reach or how they respond. “While singing” can restrict maintenance without granting a free action. “While equipped” does not make the item affect all allies.

For a trigger, identify the event, eligible observer, opportunity, response and action economy. If a response spends the independent Reaction Slot, it needs an available slot and the ordinary immediate scope unless an explicit exception changes them. If it is an automatic authored change, say what actually changes and when; do not conceal an extra action inside a trigger label.

**Example authored response.** When a conscious ally within ordinary reach begins to fall and the actor can perceive it, the actor may spend an available independent Reaction Slot to attempt a catch with a free hand. Resolve actual weight or interference through the agreed procedure. This example grants no remote rescue, additional slot or guaranteed success.
Resolve applicability before stacking

items: Identify the actual acquisitions or sources, avoiding duplicated references.
Confirm each source's recipient, metric, condition and scope.
Apply stated uniqueness, caps, exclusions or nonstacking rules.
Combine the remaining contributions using their actual operation or special procedure.
Record continuing consequences independently of the resulting number.

blocks.text: Applicable contributions stack by default unless their authored rules say otherwise. This does not erase training's upgrade semantics, make repeated resistance quarter damage, or turn a reference into a purchase. Those are different kinds of contribution with explicit procedures.

When two rules contain incompatible instructions, identify the conflict and agree their interaction. Do not invent a global priority such as latest, highest BU or strongest title unless the campaign has deliberately adopted it. A future use can be revised before commitment; a surprise reinterpretation after a roll is not a reliable adjudication procedure.
Probability bias calculation

Let A be qualifying advantage stacks and D qualifying disadvantage stacks after actual exclusions. Net bias is A - D. If positive, roll net bias +1 resolution dice and keep the highest. If negative, roll its absolute value +1 and keep the lowest. If zero, roll one. Then add the applicable static bonus once. Damage dice are not automatically resolution dice.

**Checked example.** Three advantage sources and one disadvantage qualify for a check with +6. Roll 3d20: 4, 11 and 17. Keep 17 and add +6 once for 23. If the first advantage's condition fails, the same remaining sources leave one advantage: roll two dice instead. A static -2 penalty affects the +6 separately; it does not cancel an advantage stack unless its rule actually changes bias.
Floors, ceilings and fixed results

Identify whether a rule constrains the raw die, the combined check result, a bonus or an underlying stat. “Minimum final Knowledge result 10” and “minimum d20 result 10” are mechanically different. Neither changes Mental by itself.

**Example authored floor.** A trained Knowledge check has combined bonus +5 and a rule saying its final result is at least 10. A die of 2 gives 7, then the stated final-result floor gives 10. If the rule instead says the selected d20 cannot be below 10, the same roll would become die 10 plus bonus 5, totaling 15. Record which was intended before use.

A fixed result likewise needs a stated stage and scope. Explain its relationship to bias and other modifiers. If a ceiling and floor conflict, revise or agree the interaction; this reference does not prescribe a secret winning operation. Natural 20 and natural 1 have no universal automatic success/failure or damage multiplier in the default framework.
Character construction in full
Foundation procedure for a new character

items: Agree the campaign, expectations, starting level or custom BU budget and separate equipment terms.
Write a concept, purpose and connection to the party. These descriptions do not themselves grant unlisted mechanics.
Allocate base Physical, Mental and Magical. The default total is 10; each base value is -1 through +5. Keep later contributions separate from that allocation.
Choose the proficient attribute under the agreed foundation and record additional actual training grants. Use the ten current practices, not an older eighteen-skill or sliced-bonus system.
Acquire positive owned verb and domain access in the character build. Identify each permission's bound scope. Items and mirrored access alone do not satisfy that foundation requirement.
Add other useful acquisitions, keeping actual ownership, permitted additional occurrences and credit readable. Missing range/output categories use Touch and 1d4 baselines.
Organize effects, capabilities and any useful heritages. Reusing an acquisition does not charge again.
Record equipment separately, including Item BU, Load, final slots and activation conditions.
Resolve current attributes, PB, practices, saves, selected DC, maximum Vitality, movement and capacities through their actual active rules.
Establish current state, including current Vitality, remaining short-rest allowance, consequences and any ongoing work.
Test normal, stretched and outside-scope uses. Review unclear rules, prices and limits before the first tense scene.

blocks.text: The foundation permits useful ordinary competence without purchasing a catalogue action for every task. A positive Water permission is not required to lift a bucket by hand. Conversely, ordinary competence does not provide distant extraordinary water control. Use the actual intended result to identify which access matters.

ceil(maximum Vitality/2) between completed long rests; consume actual healing
